userStories.title: Whitespace-guard arithmetic mutation operators
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Stop arithmetic mutation operators from corrupting string literals, module specifiers, URLs, and paths while continuing to mutate spaced binary arithmetic.

**Motivation** — G4 — arithmetic operators have no string or comment awareness.

**Approach** — Each arithmetic pattern requires whitespace on both sides, mirroring `COMPARISON_GT` / `COMPARISON_LT`: `+` becomes `/(?<=\s)\+(?=\s)/g`, and likewise for `-`, `*`, `/`. A real binary expression (`const idx = line - 1;`) is spaced by every formatter in use; a module specifier (`"../config"`), a URL, or a path fragment is not. This was probed against three real nax source files: arithmetic candidates fell from 32 to 0, 1, and 1 respectively, and the survivors were `const idx = line - 1;` and `const lineNumber = i + 1;` — genuine off-by-one mutations, exactly the class the gate exists to inject.

**Scope** — In: update the shared arithmetic-pair regexes used by TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust; update the existing mutator tests. Out: candidate sampling and per-file budget placement belong to US-002; test-execution classification and output counts belong to US-003; runtime reporting belongs to US-004.

**Interface** — `ARITHMETIC_PAIRS` remains `ReadonlyArray<readonly [RegExp, string]>`; `generateMutants` remains `(input: GenerateMutantsInput) => Mutant[]`.
acceptanceCriteria: When `generateMutants` receives `import { NaxError } from "@/errors";` as TypeScript source, it returns no mutant with `operatorId` `ts:arith-flip`.
When `generateMutants` receives `import type { Mutant } from "./types";` as TypeScript source, it returns no mutant with `operatorId` `ts:arith-flip`.
When `generateMutants` receives `const url = "https://a.example/b/c";` as TypeScript source, it returns no mutant with `operatorId` `ts:arith-flip`.
When `generateMutants` receives `const idx = line - 1;` as TypeScript source, it returns a `ts:arith-flip` mutant whose `after` is `const idx = line + 1;`.
When `generateMutants` receives `const total = a + b;` as TypeScript source, it returns a `ts:arith-flip` mutant whose `after` is `const total = a - b;`.
When `generateMutants` receives `const half = n / 2;` as TypeScript source, it returns a `ts:arith-flip` mutant whose `after` is `const half = n * 2;`.
When `generateMutants` receives `const twice = n * 2;` as TypeScript source, it returns a `ts:arith-flip` mutant whose `after` is `const twice = n / 2;`.
When `generateMutants` receives `y = a + b` as Python source, it returns a `py:arith-flip` mutant whose `after` is `y = a - b`.
When `generateMutants` receives `path = "a/b/c"` as Python source, it returns no mutant with `operatorId` `py:arith-flip`.
When `generateMutants` receives `sum := a + b` as Go source, it returns a `go:arith-flip` mutant whose `after` is `sum := a - b`.
When `generateMutants` receives `let sum = a + b;` as Rust source, it returns a `rust:arith-flip` mutant whose `after` is `let sum = a - b;`.
Given TypeScript source with five relative-specifier import lines followed by spaced arithmetic, when `generateMutants` runs, every returned mutant has `line` greater than or equal to 6.
When `generateMutants` is called twice with identical `source`, `language`, and `file`, it returns deeply equal arrays.

routing.reasoning: A focused shared-regex behavior change with existing unit-test coverage and no new abstraction.

userStories.title: Evenly sample mutation candidates across changed files
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace source-order and first-file-only mutation truncation with a deterministic even-spread sample across all changed files.

**Motivation** — G1 — the budget is spent on the top of the file.

**Approach** — A new exported `selectEvenlySpaced(mutants, max)` in `src/verification/mutation/select.ts` takes the full candidate list and returns `max` entries at a fixed stride (`stride = floor(length / max)`, indices `0, stride, 2*stride, …`). `generateMutants` loses its early-break so it returns every candidate for a file; `mutationCheckOp` gathers candidates across **all** changed files, then applies `selectEvenlySpaced` once to the combined list. This fixes both biases in one place — top-of-file and first-file-only — and keeps selection a pure, deterministic function.

Selection cannot guarantee a buildable mutant, and it does not try to. That is what G2 is for: a mutant that lands on a type annotation is now reported as `errored` and discarded rather than counted as `killed`.

**Scope** — In: add the pure selector, export it, remove `generateMutants` early truncation, make the operation select after reading all candidate files, and preserve the all-zero `outcomes` contract for an empty selection. Out: whitespace guards are US-001; evidence-based classification and nonzero outcome aggregation belong to US-003; runtime collection and reporting belong to US-004.

**Interface** — `selectEvenlySpaced(mutants, max)` is exported from `src/verification/mutation/select.ts`; `generateMutants` remains `(input: GenerateMutantsInput) => Mutant[]`.
acceptanceCriteria: When imported from `src/verification/mutation/select.ts`, `selectEvenlySpaced` is callable as a function.
When `selectEvenlySpaced` receives nine mutants and `max` 3, it returns exactly three mutants.
When `selectEvenlySpaced` receives nine mutants and `max` 3, it returns input positions 0, 3, and 6.
When `selectEvenlySpaced` receives ten mutants and `max` 3, it returns input positions 0, 3, and 6.
When `selectEvenlySpaced` receives two mutants and `max` 5, it returns both mutants in input order.
When `selectEvenlySpaced` receives an empty list and `max` 3, it returns an empty array.
When `selectEvenlySpaced` receives nine mutants and `max` 0, it returns an empty array.
When `selectEvenlySpaced` receives nine mutants and `max` -1, it returns an empty array.
When `selectEvenlySpaced` is called twice with the same input and `max`, it returns deeply equal arrays.
When `generateMutants` receives source yielding more than three candidates with no `max`, it returns every candidate rather than truncating.

Given mutation checking with `maxMutants` 2, one changed file with at least six candidates, and regression returning `TEST_FAILURE` with `failCount` 1, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, it invokes regression exactly twice.

Given mutation checking with `maxMutants` 2, two changed files each with at least six candidates, and regression returning `SUCCESS`, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, its two survivors have distinct `file` values.
Given mutation checking with one changed file that yields no candidates, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, it never invokes regression.
Given mutation checking with no candidates after selection, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, it returns `success: true`, empty survivors, all-zero outcomes, and runs no tests.

routing.reasoning: This adds a pure selection abstraction and rewires candidate gathering across the mutation operation while preserving fail-open behavior.

outOfScope: Restricting mutant candidates to the story's changed diff lines (gap analysis G3). Mutants continue to be drawn from whole changed files; scoping them to added and modified hunks requires threading diff hunk ranges into `generateMutants` and is deferred to a follow-up arc.

userStories.title: Classify unexecuted test failures as errored
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Require evidence of executed tests before reporting a mutation as killed, and expose all three outcome totals from the operation.

**Motivation** — G2 — unbuildable mutants are classified `killed`.

**Approach** — On the `TEST_FAILURE` arm, `classifyMutant` returns `killed` only when there is evidence tests actually executed — `(passCount ?? 0) + (failCount ?? 0) > 0`. With no such evidence the mutant produced a non-zero exit with no test results, which means compilation, module resolution, or collection failed: `errored`. All other arms are unchanged.

This is deliberately conservative in one further case: a genuine test failure whose output the parser cannot recognise (an unknown framework format) now classifies as `errored` rather than `killed`. Discarding an inconclusive result is correct for a spot-check; the current behaviour claims a kill it cannot substantiate, which is the exact false all-clear this spec exists to remove.

The op gains `outcomes: { killed, survived, errored }` so the three-way distinction is observable rather than inferred from an empty `survivors` array.

**Scope** — In: modify only mutation-specific classification and operation aggregation; update existing tests that encode old no-count kills. Out: parser changes are not part of this story; candidate selection is US-002; runtime reporting is US-004.

**Interface** — `classifyMutant` remains `(result: VerificationResult) => MutantOutcome`; `VerificationResult` is unchanged and already carries optional `passCount`, `failCount`; `MutationCheckOutput` becomes `{ success: true; survivors: readonly SurvivingMutant[]; outcomes: { killed: number; survived: number; errored: number } }`.

**Modifies** — this story changes the meaning of `TEST_FAILURE` for the classifier, and two existing assertions encode the old meaning. The implementer is authorised to edit both files; without this the story deadlocks with a correct implementation against tests it may not touch.

- `test/unit/verification/mutation/classify.test.ts` — its `makeResult` helper builds a `VerificationResult` with no `passCount` or `failCount`. Two assertions consequently break: `AC3: TEST_FAILURE -> killed` and `AC3: accepts a VerificationResult with only status populated`, both expecting `killed` from a result carrying no test counts. Under the new rule both inputs classify as `errored`. Update these two cases to supply `failCount` where the intent is `killed`, and add the no-counts case as an `errored` expectation.
- `test/unit/operations/mutation-check.test.ts` — the `AC4: TEST_FAILURE kills the mutant` case stubs `regression` with a `TEST_FAILURE` result carrying no counts. Its assertion (empty `survivors`) still passes, but for the wrong reason: the mutant is now `errored`, not `killed`. Add `failCount: 1` to that stub so the case exercises a genuine kill.
acceptanceCriteria: When `classifyMutant` receives `TEST_FAILURE` with `passCount` 0 and `failCount` 0, it returns `errored`.
When `classifyMutant` receives `TEST_FAILURE` with both `passCount` and `failCount` absent, it returns `errored`.
When `classifyMutant` receives `TEST_FAILURE` with `passCount` 0 and `failCount` 1, it returns `killed`.
When `classifyMutant` receives `TEST_FAILURE` with `passCount` 5 and `failCount` 2, it returns `killed`.
When `classifyMutant` receives `SUCCESS`, it returns `survived`.
When `classifyMutant` receives `TIMEOUT`, it returns `errored`.
When `classifyMutant` receives `ENVIRONMENTAL_FAILURE`, it returns `errored`.
When `classifyMutant` receives `ASSET_CHECK_FAILED`, it returns `errored`.
Given one candidate and regression returning `TEST_FAILURE` with both counts 0, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, `outcomes.errored` is 1.
Given one candidate and regression returning `TEST_FAILURE` with both counts 0, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, `outcomes.killed` is 0.
Given one candidate and regression returning `TEST_FAILURE` with `failCount` 1, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, `outcomes.killed` is 1.
Given one candidate and regression returning `SUCCESS`, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, `outcomes.survived` is 1.
Given one candidate and regression returning `TEST_FAILURE` with both counts 0, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, `survivors` has length 0.

routing.reasoning: A contained behavioral contract correction across classifier and operation output, with existing tests requiring deliberate semantic updates.

userStories.title: Surface mutation survivors at run completion
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist per-story mutation results on the run runtime and visibly report survivors at run end.

**Motivation** — G5 — surviving mutants have no consumer.

**Approach** — `mutationCheckOp` records its per-story result into `ctx.runtime.mutationSummaries`, a `Map<string, MutationStorySummary>` on `NaxRuntime`. `runCompletionPhase` reads the map at run end, logs a warning when any survivor exists, and in headless non-`json` mode prints a formatted block — mirroring how `outputAdvisoryFindingsSummary` handles sub-threshold review findings. `json` mode stays silent, consistent with the advisory precedent.

The survivors are **not** converted into `Finding` objects. `FindingSource` is a closed nine-member union and `AdvisoryFindingSummaryEntry.reviewer` is `"semantic" | "adversarial"`; both are review-owned, and routing a deterministic operation's output through the review-audit sink would widen shared review contracts to carry something that is not a review. The dedicated collector keeps the blast radius inside the mutation feature.

**Scope** — In: define and initialize the runtime collector, record outputs when `storyId` is present, add a pure log-format formatter and barrel export, log survivors at completion, and print only in headless non-JSON mode. Out: classifier/outcome production is US-003; converting mutation output to Findings or review-audit data is excluded.

**Interface** — `NaxRuntime` gains `mutationSummaries: Map<string, MutationStorySummary>`; `formatMutationSummary` is exported from `src/log-format/mutation-summary.ts` and remains pure, returning a string without stdout writes; `runCompletionPhase` remains `(options: RunnerCompletionOptions) => Promise<RunnerCompletionResult>`.
acceptanceCriteria: When imported from `src/log-format/mutation-summary.ts`, `formatMutationSummary` is callable as a function.
When `formatMutationSummary` receives one story summary with one survivor, its string contains that survivor's file path.
When `formatMutationSummary` receives one story summary with one survivor, its string contains that survivor's line number.
When `formatMutationSummary` receives one story summary with one survivor, its string contains that survivor's `operatorId`.
When `formatMutationSummary` receives one story summary with one survivor, its string contains that story ID.
When `formatMutationSummary` receives an empty collection of summaries, it returns an empty string.
When `formatMutationSummary` receives summaries with only killed and errored counts and empty survivors, it returns an empty string.
When `formatMutationSummary` receives two summaries each with a survivor, its string contains the second survivor's file path.
Given `storyId` `US-007`, one candidate, and regression returning `SUCCESS`, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, `runtime.mutationSummaries` contains key `US-007` with one survivor.
Given no `storyId` in the call context, when `mutationCheckOp` executes, `runtime.mutationSummaries` remains empty.
Given headless normal mode and a runtime summary with a survivor, when `runCompletionPhase` executes, standard output contains that survivor's file path.
Given headless JSON mode and a runtime summary with a survivor, when `runCompletionPhase` executes, standard output does not contain that survivor's file path.
Given headless normal mode and an empty runtime mutation summary map, when `runCompletionPhase` executes, standard output does not contain `surviving mutant`.
Given a runtime summary with one survivor, when `runCompletionPhase` executes, it emits a warning log record whose data has survivor count 1.

routing.reasoning: The change wires one existing operation result through the established runtime collector and headless formatter patterns across five clear, bounded modules.

outOfScope: Converting surviving mutants into `Finding` objects or routing them through the review-audit sink. The run-end summary is the only consumer this spec adds.

Promoting the gate from advisory to blocking, or feeding surviving mutants back to the implementer as a rectification finding. The design defers this behind observed false-alarm data, which does not yet exist.

analysis:
This is an enhancement of the existing advisory mutation spot-check, not a greenfield feature. The mutation pipeline is split between operator tables, candidate generation, outcome classification, and the deterministic operation. `ARITHMETIC_PAIRS` currently uses unguarded global regexes in `src/verification/mutation/operators.ts:105-110`; the comparison operators at `src/verification/mutation/operators.ts:37-44` already demonstrate whitespace-scoped lookarounds. `generateMutants` in `src/verification/mutation/mutator.ts:29-61` processes lines and operators deterministically but honours an optional `max` with an early break, so it returns first-in-source-order candidates. `mutationCheckOp.execute` in `src/operations/mutation-check.ts:66-183` compounds that bias by stopping collection once it reaches `cfg.maxMutants` before it reaches later changed files; it applies/reverts every selected mutant in a fail-open loop and currently only retains survivors. `classifyMutant` in `src/verification/mutation/classify.ts:13-31` maps all `TEST_FAILURE` results to `killed`, despite `VerificationResult` already exposing optional `passCount` and `failCount` at `src/verification/types.ts:44-56`; `src/verification/runners.ts:94-106` populates those fields on runner failures. The mutation types at `src/verification/mutation/types.ts:9-25` already provide MutantOutcome and SurvivingMutant, so the output can add a typed count object without widening shared verification status types. The mutation barrel (`src/verification/mutation/index.ts`) is the integration export point for a new selector. Existing operation tests are in `test/unit/operations/mutation-check.test.ts`; classifier and mutator tests mirror their source directories under `test/unit/verification/mutation/`. The existing TEST_FAILURE operation test currently omits counts, so it must be corrected to continue exercising a real kill under the new evidence rule.

Run-end integration should remain separate from the review findings system. `NaxRuntime` declares per-run mutable collectors at `src/runtime/index.ts:110-146` and constructs them at `src/runtime/index.ts:264-297`; add a Map keyed by story ID alongside adversarial/semantic iteration maps. `CallContext` already carries runtime to `mutationCheckOp`, so recording must be conditional when storyId is absent. `runCompletionPhase` at `src/execution/runner-completion.ts:111-377` gets its logger through `getSafeLogger`, reads runtime state, logs advisory review findings, and in headless non-JSON mode dynamically imports the formatter before outputting the footer. This is the correct consumer for the mutation collector, without changing status.json or making the advisory gate blocking. `outputAdvisoryFindingsSummary` at `src/execution/lifecycle/headless-formatter.ts:91-103` establishes the required stdout policy: no output for empty data or JSON mode. `src/log-format/index.ts:8-23` is the barrel to re-export a new pure `formatMutationSummary`; keep it distinct from `src/log-format/formatter.ts` because that file is near the repository size limit. `test/unit/execution/runner-completion-events.test.ts` supplies injectable completion dependencies and option builders suited to testing logger/stdout integration.

Compatibility and migration: the gate remains opt-in, advisory, and `success: true` on every existing fail-open path. No config migration, change to the `enabled: false` default, test-runner parser modification, status.json schema change, telemetry migration, or review-Finding union expansion is required. The observable output contract adds `outcomes` to MutationCheckOutput and the runtime contract adds `mutationSummaries`; update internal test/mocks that construct these values. Selection changes only which candidates run under a capped budget, but must be deterministic. A build/collection failure with no parsed executions intentionally changes from a claimed kill to errored; existing callers should use outcomes rather than infer kills from an empty survivors list. Maintain positional revert behavior and the existing per-mutant scoped-test calculation because they are outside this feature.
outOfScope: Restricting mutant candidates to the story's changed diff lines (gap analysis G3). Mutants continue to be drawn from whole changed files; scoping them to added and modified hunks requires threading diff hunk ranges into `generateMutants` and is deferred to a follow-up arc.

Creating the dedicated `test/unit/verification/mutation/operators.test.ts` covering every shipped operator id (gap analysis G6). This spec tests only the arithmetic operators it changes; six of sixteen operator ids remain without direct coverage.

Hoisting the loop-invariant `selectScopedTests` call out of the per-mutant loop in `mutationCheckOp` (gap analysis G8). The redundant per-mutant recomputation is a performance concern, not a correctness one.
Making `revertMutant` verify the target line still holds the mutated content before restoring it (gap analysis G9). Positional revert remains as shipped.
Adding a `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` handler that reverts an in-flight mutant (gap analysis G10). An interrupted run can still leave a mutated source file in the worktree.
Changing the `enabled: false` default, enabling the gate in nax's own `.nax/config.json`, or adding run telemetry counters for kill rate and false-alarm rate (gap analysis G12).
Deduplicating mutants across operators and detecting semantically equivalent mutants (gap analysis G13).
Running mutants in parallel, adding an aggregate time budget, or accounting mutation cost in the run's cost reporting (gap analysis G14).

Promoting the gate from advisory to blocking, or feeding surviving mutants back to the implementer as a rectification finding. The design defers this behind observed false-alarm data, which does not yet exist.
Converting surviving mutants into `Finding` objects or routing them through the review-audit sink. The run-end summary is the only consumer this spec adds.
Restricting mutation of type-only positions such as type annotations and generic parameters. Mutants landing there are reported as `errored` rather than prevented.
